title: TRUE or FALSE? Jaws & Disney Lied To You About These 12 Animals
blurb: TRUE or FALSE? Jaws, The Lion King, Finding Nemo and Bambi taught you some "facts" that aren't true... and two that are. Guess before the 3-second timer, keep score, and drop your score out of 12 in the comments 👇
next: Subscribe for Part 4: monsters that turned out to be REAL.
pinned:
📝 SCORE CHECK: how many did you get out of 12? 👇

Answer key: TRUE = river sharks + Nemo's dad. Everything else was FALSE.

Which movie lied to YOU the most? Comment it.

beats.say: Jaws, The Lion King, Finding Nemo and Bambi all taught you animal facts. Most of them are wrong. Two are true. Can you spot them? I couldn't. I'm made of sticks.
You get three seconds to guess true or false. Keep score, and tell me your number out of twelve at the end. No cheating. I can see you. Okay, I can't. But act like I can. First up, sharks.
True or false? A shark can smell one drop of blood from a mile away.
beats.quiz:
SHARKS SMELL
BLOOD FROM
A MILE AWAY
beats.bonus: Smell has to drift to a shark on the current. If the water's flowing the wrong way, it can't smell you at all.

beats.say: False. Sharks have a great nose, but that line is wildly exaggerated. Fishing story exaggerated.
Some sharks can sense certain chemicals at about one part per million. That's roughly one drop in a bathtub. Impressive. But the ocean is a very, very big bathtub.
Bathtub? Totally. Ocean? Nope. Those are very different sizes. I checked.
beats.text:
ONE DROP.
A BATHTUB.
NOT THE OCEAN.

beats.say: And smell doesn't teleport. It has to drift to the shark on the current, which takes time. If the water's flowing the wrong way, the shark can't smell you at all. Return to sender.

What sharks are really good at is the whole package. Smell, plus feeling tiny vibrations in the water, plus sensing the electric fields from living muscles. That last one is basically a superpower. Nobody puts it on a poster.
Forget the nose. The real headline is, shark can sense your muscles. Spooky. Also kind of awesome.
So a shark is not sitting a mile away going, hmm, Kevin cut his finger. Sorry, Kevin. You're fine.
True or false? Great white sharks hunt humans.
beats.bonus: Fatal unprovoked shark bites worldwide are usually somewhere around five to ten a year.

beats.say: False. And the guy who wrote Jaws ended up feeling terrible about it.
Great whites mostly eat fish and seals. Humans are bony, low in fat, and frankly not worth the effort.
To a shark, you're basically celery. Crunchy. Disappointing. Spit it out.
Many bites on people seem to be a test bite. Basically a shark going, what is this? Nope. And then swimming away.
Your odds of being bitten by a shark are tiny. The drive to the beach is way more dangerous than the swim. The parking lot is the real Jaws.
beats.text:
THE PARKING LOT
IS THE REAL JAWS

beats.say: Plot twist. Peter Benchley, who wrote Jaws, spent years afterwards campaigning to protect sharks. That's like writing a horror movie about your neighbor and then becoming his biggest fan.
beats.text:
THE JAWS AUTHOR
BECAME A SHARK
DEFENDER

beats.say: True or false? All sharks have to keep swimming or they'll die.
beats.quiz:
ALL SHARKS MUST
KEEP SWIMMING
OR DIE
beats.bonus: Nurse sharks can pump water over their gills while lying perfectly still on the sea floor.

beats.say: False. Some do, and some take naps.
Sharks like great whites and makos mostly breathe by swimming with their mouths open, so water rushes over their gills. Those ones do need to keep moving. No breaks. No naps. Tough job.
But nurse sharks can pump water over their gills while lying perfectly still on the bottom. They just chill there like a sleepy couch cushion.
Look at this one. Zero plans today. Living the dream.
Some sharks have even been seen resting in underwater caves, lined up like they're waiting for a bus. Very calm. Dory would be furious.
So for some sharks, keep swimming is the rule. For others, it's just a suggestion.
Just keep swimming? More like, just keep snoozing.
True or false? Sharks can't get cancer.
beats.bonus: Studies of shark cartilage pills as a cancer treatment found they didn't work.

beats.say: False. Scientists have found tumors in sharks, including great whites.
The myth took off with a nineteen ninety two book called Sharks Don't Get Cancer, which helped sell a lot of shark cartilage pills.
And the cartilage fad was bad for sharks, because more demand for pills meant more sharks caught. A myth about sharks ended up hurting actual sharks.
That's like a rumor about you that somehow gets you grounded.
When those pills were actually tested on patients, they didn't work. Bad news for the pill sellers. Even worse news for the sharks.
True or false? Some sharks can swim up rivers into fresh water.
beats.bonus: Bull sharks also live in Lake Nicaragua, a freshwater lake in Central America.

beats.say: True! Meet the bull shark.
Bull sharks can handle both salt water and fresh water, which most sharks can't do. They swim up big rivers like the Amazon and the Mississippi. No passport needed.
One was reportedly caught way up the Mississippi in Illinois, more than a thousand miles from the ocean. That's not a swim. That's a road trip.
Are we there yet? Are we there yet? Said the shark, a thousand miles in.
Bull sharks have also been found living in Lake Nicaragua, a freshwater lake in Central America. A shark in a lake. Sleep well.
So if you've ever thought, at least there are no sharks in the river. Mostly true. Mostly.
True or false? Goldfish only grow to fit their bowl, so a small bowl is fine.
beats.quiz:
GOLDFISH GROW
TO FIT THE BOWL,
SO IT'S FINE
beats.bonus: Goldfish can live for decades in good conditions. Some have been recorded at over forty years old.

beats.say: False. A small bowl doesn't make a goldfish politely stay small. It makes it sick.
In a tiny bowl, the water fills up with waste fast, and the stress and bad water stunt the fish's growth. That's not a feature. That's the fish struggling.
Given a big pond, goldfish can grow longer than your hand, sometimes more than a foot long, and live for decades. Your goldfish could outlive your phone. Several phones.
Plot twist. Your tiny pet is a big fish stuck in a small apartment.
If you want a happy goldfish, it needs a proper tank with a filter, room to swim, and clean water. Basically the opposite of the bowl from every cartoon ever.
So if your goldfish lives in a bowl, it's not small because it's comfy. It's small because it's stuck.
True or false? Alligators live in the New York City sewers.
beats.bonus: Alligators are cold-blooded, and New York winters are way too cold for them to live in the sewers.

beats.say: False. But the story has a real start.
In nineteen thirty five, newspapers reported that some teenagers in New York pulled an alligator out of a sewer opening. Nobody knows for sure how it got there, maybe a pet someone got rid of.
But alligators are cold-blooded, and New York sewers are cold, dark, and short on food. There's no hidden alligator family living down there.
The legend got so famous that sewer gators ended up in comics and cartoons. The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles even have a sewer alligator buddy called Leatherhead. Great show. Terrible biology.
Alligators want warm swamps and sunshine, not subway rats and pizza crusts. Picture a gator in a tiny scarf, shivering. Sad. Very sad.
No sun? No swamp? No thank you. Gators have standards.
True or false? Hyenas are just scavengers that steal other animals' food.
beats.quiz:
HYENAS JUST
STEAL OTHER
ANIMALS' FOOD
beats.bonus: Spotted hyena clans are led by females, and the females are usually bigger than the males.

beats.say: False. The Lion King did hyenas dirty.
Spotted hyenas are excellent hunters. In many places, they catch most of their own food.
And here's the twist. Lions often steal food from hyenas, not just the other way around. Plot twist of the savanna.
Imagine cooking dinner, and the king just walks in and eats it. Rude.
Spotted hyenas also live in big family groups called clans, led by females, and they are surprisingly smart at teamwork and problem solving. Not a single one sounds like Whoopi Goldberg, though.
So the movie had the thief the wrong way round. Hyenas deserve an apology. And a better publicist.
beats.text:
THE MOVIE GOT
THE THIEF
BACKWARDS

beats.say: True or false? Male lions do most of the hunting.
beats.quiz:
MALE LIONS DO
MOST OF THE
HUNTING
beats.bonus: A male lion's roar can be heard from about five miles away.

beats.say: False. In a pride, the lionesses do most of the hunting.
The females work together as a team to bring down prey, then the big guy often shows up and eats first.
She hunts. He eats first. Nobody does the dishes.
To be fair, male lions do hunt sometimes, especially big animals like buffalo, and they defend the pride's territory. But day to day dinner? That's mostly the ladies.
Lions also sleep a ridiculous amount, often up to twenty hours a day. Twenty! I can't sit still for twenty seconds.
So the king of the jungle is mostly the king of showing up at dinnertime.
beats.text:
KING OF
SHOWING UP
FOR DINNER

beats.say: True or false? In real life, Nemo's dad would turn into Nemo's mom.
beats.quiz:
NEMO'S DAD WOULD
BECOME NEMO'S
MOM
beats.bonus: Clownfish live safely among sea anemone tentacles thanks to a protective slime coat on their skin.

beats.say: True. Finding Nemo skipped the weirdest part.
Clownfish are all born male. In each group, the biggest fish is the female, and the second biggest is her breeding male.
If the female disappears, the male changes into a female and takes her place.
Pixar looked at that and said, maybe not in this movie. Pass the popcorn.
And Finding Nemo had another problem. Clownfish dads really do take care of the eggs, fanning them and guarding them. So Marlin being an overprotective parent? Actually accurate.
So after Nemo's mom was gone, the scientifically accurate movie is called Finding Nemo, starring his mom, Marlin.
True or false? Mother deer stay with their babies all day.
beats.quiz:
MOM DEER STAY
WITH THEIR
FAWNS ALL DAY
beats.bonus: A fawn's spotted coat helps it disappear into sun-dappled grass and leaves.

beats.say: False. Mom deer leave their fawns alone for hours, on purpose.
A young fawn has very little scent and spotted camouflage, so hiding it quietly in the grass is safer than having mom stand around next to it.
Look at this little loaf. Hiding champion. Barely any scent, full spots, maximum stillness.
She comes back a few times a day to feed it. So if you find a fawn on its own, it's almost always fine. Leave it where it is.
People sometimes pick up fawns thinking they are rescuing them, and that actually causes real problems. The best rescue is usually walking away and letting mom come back.
It's not abandoned. It's at daycare. Very quiet daycare. The snack schedule is excellent.
True or false? Mice love cheese more than anything.
beats.quiz:
MICE LOVE
CHEESE MORE
THAN ANYTHING
beats.bonus: Pest experts often suggest peanut butter as mouse trap bait instead of cheese.

beats.say: False. Thanks, cartoons.
Mice mostly eat grains, seeds, and sweet stuff. Given the choice, a lot of mice would rather have peanut butter or cereal than cheese. Sorry, every cartoon ever.
Peanut butter wins. Cheese is crying in the fridge.
Nobody's totally sure where the cheese idea came from. One guess is that people used to store cheese out in the open, so mice found it easy to grab.
beats.text:
CHEESE WAS JUST
EASY TO STEAL

beats.say: Mice also nibble constantly, eating lots of tiny meals all day. They are basically the animal version of snacking at midnight.
So if you set a trap with cheese, the mouse might just walk past it and go eat your cereal. Then leave you a thank you crumb.

Scores! The true ones were the river sharks and Nemo's dad. Everything else was false. Drop your score out of twelve in the comments, and tell me which one got you. Twelve out of twelve? Show off. I love it.
And subscribe, because next time we're going after monsters that turned out to be real. Yes, some of them are real.
